title: Small farms face H-2A application and compliance paperwork; burden estimates are disputed

history.reason: Signal from DOL final rule and public comments.

Review correction: separated proposal dispute/final four-hour incremental familiarization estimate from total H-2A filing burden; qualified matched-subset small-employer statistics and documented enforcement-scope limits.

description: H-2A employers file job orders, certification applications and addenda. The 2024 rule’s economic analysis models incremental rule familiarization and added application disclosures, not the full seasonal application or compliance workload; a commenter disputed the proposal’s incremental estimates.
customer_segment: H-2A employers, including small farms. DOL classified 2,159 of 2,615 matched employers as small (82.5%); those matches came from 9,927 unique employers excluding labor contractors in FY2020/FY2021 data. Match coverage does not establish population-wide prevalence.
context: Historical April 2024 final-rule analysis. The DOL rule page describes an August 2024 injunction limiting enforcement in specified states/entities; later litigation and all subsequent policy changes have not been comprehensively checked. Do not assume the 2024 additions apply universally today.

evidence.text: Among 9,927 unique H-2A employers excluding labor contractors in FY2020/FY2021 data, DOL matched employee/revenue data for 2,615; 2,159 matches (82.5%) were small, averaging 11 employees and about $3.6 million annual revenue. This is a matched subset, not a representative prevalence estimate for all H-2A employers.

An industry commenter disputed the proposal’s incremental familiarization/new-disclosure estimates, characterizing them as $54 and $108. These are not estimates of the full H-2A seasonal application cost.
H-2A employers may spend material staff time or consultant fees on applications and records.

In the final rule DOL increased modeled one-time rule familiarization to four hours, using an HR-specialist compensation basis. The analysis separately models added application disclosure work; neither measure is the whole H-2A application workload.

DOL’s Farmworker Protection Rule page describes an August 26, 2024 preliminary injunction prohibiting enforcement in specified states and against specified entities. This is a documented scope restriction, not a comprehensive current legal-status review.

alternatives: Agricultural labor contractors, associations and attorneys who file on behalf of farms: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: The proposal’s disputed figures address incremental changes, so they cannot support a comparison with total seasonal filing/agent costs. DOL revised familiarization to four hours in the final rule. This source alone does not establish either low or high total employer pain.
The small-employer proportion is conditional on successful matching, with labor contractors excluded; selection and coverage limit generalization to the full employer population.

uncertainty: Unknown: total actual seasonal time and fees, avoidable residual work, representativeness of matched employers, agent usage and existing automation, software buyer, and complete current rule/litigation status. No willingness-to-pay evidence.
open_questions: What do H-2A employers or their agents actually spend per season?
Do agents already automate this work?
next_actions: Find independent data on H-2A filing cost and agent usage.
